filename: Systematic LLM Translation of Legacy Scientific Code to Differentiable Frameworks_ Application to a Land Surface Model.pdf
title: Systematic LLM Translation of Legacy Scientific Code to Differentiable Frameworks: Application to a Land Surface Model
processes: Canopy sensible and latent heat fluxes
ml_methods: Large Language Model agents (Claude / Claude Opus 4.6)
parameterization_target: Multilayer canopy land surface processes and flux parameterizations
code_availability: Both the translated model and pipeline infrastructure are stated as released as a reusable framework, though specific repository URLs are omitted in the main text.
testbed_rationale: The study produces an end-to-end differentiable land surface model (clm-ml-jax) and agentic translation pipeline rather than a standardized benchmark dataset for training or evaluating ML parameterizations.
pain_points: Branch evaluation in JAX (jnp.where) evaluating both branches, generating NaN gradients (0 x inf) with division or fractional powers when x=0
Gradient explosion (|J|^N -> infinity) in iterative solvers (e.g., Obukhov length secant solver and stomatal conductance bisection) requiring implicit function theorem (IFT) adjoint reformulation
Tracing and compilation bottlenecks: dynamic closures triggering continuous XLA recompilations (approx. 290 s per call) and flat LLVM graph explosion on CPU vmap requiring GPU execution
Autodiff tape silently broken by standard Python type casts (e.g., float()) and local variable bindings
Agentic laziness and lack of persistent cross-session state in long autonomous agent loops
extraction_notes: Work funded by NSF LEAP STC (Award #2019625). While primarily a code translation and differentiable programming study, it evaluates gradient-based parameter calibration (L-BFGS-B and Adam) on land surface parameters (Vcmax25, stomatal efficiency, Tref).
